ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is labeled trans-1,2-dichloroethene, and the two C–Cl bonds are located on opposite sides of the planar alkene C=C: one Cl is at the lower left, and the other Cl is at the upper right. The right side of the figure is labeled cis-1,2-dichloroethene, and the two C–Cl bonds are located on the same side of the C=C, both above. Reasoning: The bond dipole of the C–Cl bond points toward the more electronegative chlorine atom. In the trans structure, the directions of the two C–Cl bond dipoles are opposite, and overall they mostly cancel each other, so the molecule's net dipole moment is very small or close to zero. In the cis structure, the two C–Cl bond dipoles face the same side and reinforce each other, producing a larger net dipole moment. Therefore cis-1,2-dichloroethene is more polar, the intermolecular dipole-dipole interactions are stronger, and more energy is needed to boil, so the boiling point is higher.

Then assign C–Cl bond dipoles toward chlorine. In the trans structure these dipoles largely cancel, giving little or no net dipole; in the cis structure they reinforce, giving a larger net dipole. Conclude that cis is more polar, has stronger intermolecular dipole-dipole forces, and therefore has the higher boiling point.

method.CoT_raw:
Image description first: The diagram shows two planar 1,2-dichloroethene structures. In the trans isomer on the left, the two chlorine atoms are on opposite sides of the C=C double bond, with one Cl below one carbon and the other Cl above the other carbon; the hydrogens are also on opposite sides. In the cis isomer on the right, both chlorine atoms are on the same side of the double bond, while both hydrogens are on the other side.

Reasoning: Chlorine is more electronegative than carbon and hydrogen, so each C-Cl bond has a bond dipole pointing toward chlorine. In the cis structure, the two C-Cl bond dipoles point generally in the same direction, toward the same side of the molecule, so they reinforce each other and create a net permanent molecular dipole. In the trans structure, the molecule is more symmetrical: the C-Cl bond dipoles are arranged on opposite sides and largely cancel. Therefore cis-1,2-dichloroethene is more polar than trans-1,2-dichloroethene. More polar molecules have stronger dipole-dipole intermolecular attractions, so more energy is needed to separate cis molecules during boiling.
